375: Overtaking-prohibited zones and places where you must come to a complete stop are prescribed differently. Inside tunnels, on bridges, steep downhill slopes, and curved sections of the road are overtaking-prohibited zones. An intersection where traffic is not being controlled and left and right cannot be checked or where traffic is heavy, and a place designated with traffic signs by the Commissioner of the City/Provincial Police Agency who deems it necessary to prevent danger on the road and to secure the safety and smooth flow of traffic, are places where you must come to a complete stop. (Road Traffic Act Article 31 paragraph 2)
376: Enforcement Rule of the Road Traffic Act Article 19 subparagraph 1. When the maximum speed is set by a variable speed limit sign, you must follow it, and when the maximum speed set by a variable speed limit sign differs from the maximum speed set by another traffic sign, you must follow the variable speed limit sign.
377: Every driver of a vehicle or streetcar must, when intending to pass through a railroad crossing, come to a complete stop before the crossing, confirm safety, and then pass. (Road Traffic Act Article 24, Passage of Railroad Crossings)
378: Sudden braking increases the risk of an accident with the vehicle behind. If you decelerate suddenly near an interchange and come out onto an ordinary road, your sense of speed becomes dull, so you must slow down in advance and drive at the regulation speed of the ordinary road. If you pass the interchange you should exit at, you must use the next interchange to exit.
379: Enforcement Decree of the Road Traffic Act Table 2. When turning left, crossing, making a U-turn, or changing course to the left while proceeding in the same direction, upon reaching a point at least 30 meters (100 meters on a highway) before the point where you intend to perform the act (at the edge of the intersection when turning left), extend the left arm horizontally out of the left side of the vehicle body, or extend the right arm out of the right side of the vehicle body and bend the elbow to raise it vertically, or operate the left turn signal or lights.
380: When the driver intends to turn right, the driver extends the left arm out of the left side of the vehicle body and bends the elbow to raise it vertically.
381: When the signal or instruction indicated by a traffic safety facility differs from the signal or instruction of a police officer, etc. for traffic control, you must follow the signal or instruction of the police officer, etc.
382: On the side with the yellow dashed line, you may overtake by crossing the center line, but on the side with the yellow solid line, you may not overtake by crossing the center line.
383: Road Traffic Act Article 24 (Passage of Railroad Crossings) (1) Every driver of a vehicle or streetcar who intends to pass through a railroad crossing (hereinafter crossing) must come to a complete stop before the crossing, confirm that it is safe, and then pass. However, when following the signal indicated by a traffic light, etc., the driver may pass without stopping. (2) Every driver of a vehicle or streetcar must not enter a crossing while the crossing barrier is down or about to come down, or while the crossing alarm is sounding.
384: Enforcement Decree of the Road Traffic Act [Table 2] Timing and Method of Signals. When intending to change course, operate the turn signal upon reaching a point at least 30 meters before that point.
385: You must follow the variable speed limit sign.
386: For highways, the Commissioner General of the National Police Agency, and for roads other than highways, the Commissioner of the City/Provincial Police Agency, is the authority regulating speed.
387: At a red signal, stop immediately before the stop line, and at a yellow signal before reaching the intersection, you must also stop immediately before the stop line.
388: When turning right at an intersection, even if the pedestrian signal light of the crosswalk on the right-side road is green, you may pass within the range that does not obstruct the passage of pedestrians. However, if a vehicle auxiliary signal light is installed on the side of the pedestrian signal light, passing when the auxiliary signal light is red may constitute a signal violation, so you may not pass; and if a pedestrian is on the crosswalk, you may not pass because it obstructs the pedestrian's passage even if the proceeding vehicle and the pedestrian are far apart.
389: A signal must be given upon reaching a point at least 30 meters (100 meters on a highway) before the point where you intend to perform the act (at the edge of the intersection when turning left), and you must reduce speed in advance and enter the first lane or the left-turn lane while slowing down. Enforcement Rule of the Motor Vehicle Management Act Article 2 (Classification of Motor Vehicle Types, Table 1 Types of Motor Vehicles).
390: When there is distance from the following vehicle, change lanes while maintaining speed, and when it is approaching, reduce speed and let the vehicle behind pass first.
391: (1) Among the lines dividing lanes, a solid line is a line where lane changes cannot be made. (2) A dashed line is a line where lane changes can be made. (3) Where a solid line and a dashed line run parallel, a lane change from the solid line side toward the dashed line direction is not possible. (4) Where a solid line and a dashed line run parallel, a lane change from the dashed line side toward the solid line direction is possible.
392: When the red light is flashing, a vehicle or horse must, where there is a stop line or crosswalk, come to a complete stop immediately before it or immediately before the intersection, and then may proceed while paying attention to other traffic.
393: At a place with an unprotected left turn sign, you may turn left while paying attention to other traffic when the green light is on. If you collide with an oncoming straight-proceeding vehicle while turning left on the green light, the left-turning vehicle becomes the at-fault party in a minor-negligence ordinary accident.
394: The minimum speed on a highway is uniformly prescribed as 50 kilometers per hour on all highways, and on a motor-vehicle-only road, both a maximum speed and a minimum speed are limited. On ordinary roads, there is no minimum speed limit, and the maximum speed on a highway with two or more lanes each way is prescribed differently depending on the vehicle type.
395: A yellow solid line prohibits overtaking; inside tunnels and on bridges are overtaking-prohibited places, and it is prescribed that overtaking cannot be done when the vehicle ahead is overtaking another vehicle.
